activities.anchor: An X-ray tube is a vacuum tube with two ends
activities.caption: rebuild the production sequence
activities.name: radTubeOrder

config.prompt: Inside the tube — put the production sequence in order:
items: the filament is heated until electrons boil off it — thermionic emission
the kilovoltage peak (kVp) accelerates them across the gap
they slam into the spinning tungsten anode at around half the speed of light
the sudden deceleration releases the energy as X-ray photons
config.why: A vacuum tube with two ends: cathode to anode, and every photon the patient receives begins as this conversion of electrical energy.

activities.caption: pair each spectral term with its mechanism
activities.name: radSpectrumMatch

config.prompt: The tube's two photon factories — pair each term:

pairs.right: an electron skims past a tungsten nucleus and radiates whatever it lost — a continuous spectrum up to the kVp
an outer-shell electron falls into a knocked-out vacancy, emitting a photon of precise energy
high atomic number, high melting point
softer energies that contrast soft tissue better

config.why: The continuous spectrum is the honest signature of random braking; the characteristic lines depend on the target material.

activities.anchor: As the beam crosses the body
activities.caption: file each fact under its interaction
activities.name: radInteractSort

config.prompt: Two mechanisms make the image — file each fact:

items.label: a photon fully absorbed, an electron ejected
scales steeply with atomic number — approximately as the cube
a photon deflected, sharing its energy
depends mostly on electron density; dominates at higher energies
photons flying in all directions that fog the image

config.why: Contrast comes from photoelectric absorption; fog comes from Compton scatter — which is why grids and collimation exist.

activities.anchor: that an X-ray machine is a kind of camera
activities.caption: find the faulty line — an imaging briefing
activities.name: radCameraSpot

config.prompt: One line of this briefing on how the image forms is wrong — click it:
lines: Nothing returns to the machine: the detector sits behind the patient.
The image is made by what gets through, which is why the discipline is called projection imaging.
The patient is positioned between tube and detector.
The machine photographs the inside by detecting rays bounced back from the tissue.
config.correction: Nothing bounces back — the shadow is cast by what gets through, and the detector records it from behind the patient.
config.why: The shadow can only be as good as the beam that casts it — which is why thickness, positioning and penetration matter so much.

config.prompt: A chest radiograph is about 0.02 mSv; a CT abdomen is roughly 8 mSv. Roughly how many chest radiographs equal one CT abdomen?
config.why: About 400 — and for context, average natural background is around 2.4 mSv per year. The comparisons do not make dose trivial; they make justification and optimisation meaningful.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — what actually accumulates
activities.name: radCumulCloze

config.text: The photons pass through or are absorbed and are gone in fractions of a second. What is genuinely cumulative is the %%0%%: each exposure adds a small increment of lifetime %%1%% risk, which is why dose history is recorded.
config.hint: First blank: what kind of bookkeeping adds up. Second: the no-threshold category of harm.

activities.anchor: The exposure arithmetic deserves one fully worked passage
activities.caption: drag the divider — two resolved trades
activities.name: radTradeCompare

config.prompt: Technique charts store resolved trades — drag the divider.

before.label: Large patient, cannot hold still
before.text: Raise kVp by 15 per cent (60 to 69) — receptor exposure roughly doubles, so mAs drops to 2.5: higher penetration, half the dose quantity, half the exposure time, and half the motion-blur risk.

after.label: Thin, still patient, fine-detail view
after.text: Lower kVp for maximal subject contrast, more mAs accepted — sharp grey-scale separation beats dose economy on a milligray examination.

config.why: Every element of the trade is visible: kVp buys penetration and speed, mAs pays the dose bill, and the constraint of the case chooses where the saving lands.

activities.anchor: Three refinements take you from technique charts
activities.caption: true or false — the refinements
activities.name: radRefineJudge

statements.s: Stack identical absorbers and each one halves what is left — four halvings leave one sixteenth of the beam.
statements.why: The half-value layer's arithmetic; it is why a few tenths of a millimetre of lead apron cuts scattered radiation to a small fraction.

statements.s: The anode heel effect is exploited by placing the cathode end over thicker anatomy.
statements.why: The target's own slant absorbs part of the exit beam, so intensity varies along the anode–cathode axis.

statements.s: Iodine and barium contrast media work through the Compton effect.
statements.why: They weaponise the photoelectric effect — absorption edges tuned almost exactly to the diagnostic spectrum.

statements.s: The linear no-threshold model is an extrapolation from atomic-bomb-survivor data down to radiography's doses.
statements.why: Where epidemiology cannot resolve the risk, the profession's answer is justification frameworks and detectors that keep dropping the dose per image.
